properties.statement:
THE SETTLING MEASUREMENT for `dec:idea-the-load-bearing-prose-is-unchecked-against-the-code-it-describes`, run 2026-09-02 on Anthony's word. IT DOES NOT SAY WHAT THE FIVE INSTANCES SUGGESTED IT WOULD.

**POPULATION** — the 167 committed toolsnaps, which are the served descriptions byte-for-byte:
· 767 sentences total.
· 343 (45%) carry a marker of an assertion about behaviour (never / always / cannot / refuses / only / silently / …).
· 127 of 167 tools (76%) carry at least one.

**READ, NOT COUNTED** — a reproducible random sample of 40 (seed 20260902) was READ and classified, because dev_storyflow's own lesson from the same week is that a grep cannot tell a claim from its denial: their regex was 40% wrong on first run, matching negations like "STATUS is planned: nothing is built" on the word "built".
· ~32 of 40 (80%) make a CHECKABLE claim about what the computation does.
· 4 are advice ("Never set kpp on your own reading"), 4 are descriptive or historical ("Until this tool existed …").

SO THE ANSWER TO THE DECISION'S OWN TEST IS **HIGH HIT RATE — IT IS ONE THING, NOT THREE BUGS.** Extrapolated, roughly 270 checkable behavioural claims stand on the served surface, and nothing systematically checks any of them.

⭐ **AND THEN THE RESULT THAT REFRAMES THE WHOLE QUESTION: THE PROSE IS MOSTLY TRUE.** Five sampled claims were verified against the code and ALL FIVE HELD:
· `propose_heal` "never mutates" — takes `&self`, cannot.
· `mint_seat` "Writes NOTHING" — no graph access, no write lock, mints and returns.
· `plan_epoch` "a planned epoch REFUSES record_change" — temporal.rs:809.
· `loop_status` "an unknown contributor_id is REFUSED" — and it is PINNED BY A TEST (`an_unknown_contributor_is_refused_rather_than_answered_with_an_empty_list`).
· `seam_coverage` "every coupling is lifted to the nearest container at that level" — TRUE, and the id-prefix bug that once made it false was fixed 2026-08-30 with the measurement in the code comment.

**SO THE DEFECT RATE IS LOW AND THE DETECTION LATENCY IS THE PROBLEM.** Five known-false claims against ~270 is on the order of 2%. Every one of the five was found by a USER, weeks after it rotted, and none by sampling — which is what a low base rate plus no checking produces. The class is real; the frequency is not the thing that hurts.

⭐ **THAT CHANGES WHAT THE REPAIR SHOULD BE.** Auditing the corpus is low-yield: at ~2% a reader would wade through fifty true sentences to find one false. The generalisable answer already exists in this design's own history — `chg:the-replay-contract-is-pinned-by-a-round-trip-not-by-a-field` root-caused an earlier instance as "a stated contract maintained by hand with nothing checking it" and fixed it with a ROUND-TRIP TEST rather than a corrected sentence. `loop_status`'s contributor refusal shows the same shape working: the claim is pinned, so it cannot rot.

⚠️ BOUNDS, and they matter for anyone acting on this. FIVE verifications cannot establish a rate — they establish that the prose is not obviously rotten, which was worth knowing and was not known. The sample was 40 of 343 and only 5 were traced to code, because each trace is a manual read. Skills and gap texts were NOT surveyed, only tool descriptions. And the five known-false instances were found by users on the surfaces users actually touch, so the true rate on HEAVILY-USED prose may be higher than on the whole corpus.
